cards.title: Kindness of Strangers: Flying With Four Children
cards.body: A parent's stress about flying with four kids was eased by a fellow passenger's unexpected kindness. Small acts of consideration from strangers can make family travel dramatically easier.

cards.title: Should Parents Reveal Will Contents to Children?
cards.body: Parents often wonder whether to disclose what's in their will to adult children. While there's no obligation to share, unexpected inheritance surprises can tear families apart.

cards.title: Empty Nest: A Parent's Complicated Joy
cards.body: Sending a child to university brings mixed emotions—sadness at their departure and joy at their independence. This milestone reminds parents of their own freedom and growth.

cards.title: Family Mealtimes: Connection Beyond Food
cards.body: Eating together offers families a crucial pause to listen, share stories, and connect meaningfully. Regular mealtimes strengthen relationships and communication between parents and children.

cards.title: Tracking Children: Parental Surveillance Anxiety
cards.body: Location-tracking apps let parents monitor loved ones' safety but can create anxiety rather than peace of mind. Finding balance between monitoring and trust is crucial.

cards.title: FaceTime Between Homes: Comfort or Anxiety?
cards.body: Goodnight calls between divorced parents' homes should comfort children but sometimes create anxiety instead. How parents handle these calls significantly impacts a child's emotional well-being.

cards.title: What Children Learn From Your Tech Use
cards.body: Parents who monitor kids' screen time but freely use devices themselves send mixed messages. A parent's technology habits shape children's relationship with screens more than rules do.

cards.title: Tickling: Understanding Play and Boundaries
cards.body: While tickling appears joyful, it can sometimes cause distress rather than genuine pleasure. Understanding your child's comfort levels with physical play is essential.

cards.title: ADHD Medication Sequencing in Children
cards.body: Many children are started on antipsychotics for ADHD without trying stimulants first, which is often suboptimal. Better medication sequencing protocols could improve treatment outcomes.
